title: Health-signal gating and derated autoscaling for SLO resilience
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Scope: Harden Redwood's autoscaler and routing behavior by reworking health signal collection and introducing a 'derate' gating layer so transient probe noise or partial-region degradation does not cause autoscaler thrash, circuit-breaker-triggered cascades, or unnecessary multi-region failovers. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout for:

- Health signal sampling: move from uniform short-window checks to jittered sampling + median-filtered window aggregation per instance class.
- Gating layer: binary health-gate per node-pool (OK / DEGRADED / OUT) derived from weighted signals (readiness, latency p95/p99 spike, error-rate).
- Derated autoscaling: when pool enters DEGRADED we reduce target concurrency and increase aggregation window to prevent immediate scale-down/up oscillations. Derate factors are configurable by pool and tier.
- Circuit breaker tuning: introduce two-stage breakers: soft-break (route new requests to fallback pool, keep a % of traffic) and hard-break (full failover) with separate thresholds and cooldowns.
- Load shedding policy: graceful shedding for tail-latency cases (reject low-priority requests, return informative 429 with retry-after), and token-bucket based admission control during regional overcommit.
- Multi-region considerations: prefer regional containment first (derate and isolate) before triggering cross-region failover; failover only when capacity metric falls below threshold for 3m and health gate is OUT in >50% of pools.

Success criteria / acceptance tests:
- Synthetic stability test: under a staged node loss in region us-west-2 (simulate 30% of GPU capacity drop), autoscaler churn (scale events per minute) reduces by >=75% compared to baseline, and failover is not triggered unless sustained degradation >3m.
- SLOs preserved in healthy regions: p99 latency in fallback/healthy region must remain within 1.5x of baseline p99 and overall availability does not drop below 99.95% for the customer cohort.
- No increased tail-latency regressions in normal traffic (A/B against control for a week).

Implementation notes:
- Add a health-gate state machine in serving runtime control plane with metrics exported to prometheus: rgw_health_gate_state{pool,region}, rgw_health_gate_score, rgw_derate_factor.
- Autoscaler: implement a derate multiplier applied to target concurrency and modify evaluation window logic (exponential backoff on re-evaluation when DERATED).
- Circuit breakers: implement soft/hard threshold evaluation on aggregated error rate and latency signals (1m and 5m windows respectively).
- API/Console changes: expose pool-level health gate, derate state, and button to force-evict into hard-failover for runbook use.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag behind canary feature (tenant opt-in).
2) Internal canary on non-critical tenant pool (2 days).
3) Gradual ramp to 20% tenants with close SRE monitoring (1 week).
4) Wide rollout after no regressions and PM signoff.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: derate too aggressively causing sustained capacity loss. Mitigation: conservative default derate (0.75) and quick rollback via feature flag; canary + automated rollback heuristics.
- Risk: probe sampling window too long delaying detection of real failure. Mitigation: tiered gating where error spikes still propagate through as a first-class signal and warm fallback routes are maintained.

Links: design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a9X-health-gating-design, implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4321, load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/oz-health-gate/load-tests
comments: 2025-02-11 - Triage: met with SRE (María Gonzalez) and PM (Liam O'Connor). Agreed to prioritize derated autoscaling over immediate cross-region failover; assigned to Ethan.

2025-02-12 - Design review: posted design doc and ran through failure scenarios (probe noise, 50% host restart, API transient spikes). Feedback: add soft-breaker to avoid immediate user-visible failovers (María).
2025-02-13 - Engineering note: decided to use median-filtered 1m window with jittered sampling to reduce synchronized probe spikes. Will still surface raw signals for debugging. (Ethan)

2025-02-14 - Implementation: added health-gate state machine scaffold and metrics export. Created initial feature flag 'health-gate-derate' for canary rollout. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4321 (WIP).

2025-02-16 - Load test (stage): injected 30% node loss in us-west-2 via chaos job. Observed autoscaler baseline churn 22 events/min -> with derate prototype 5 events/min. Need to tighten cooldown logic. Captured traces and flamegraphs in linked dashboard.

2025-02-17 - Code review: María requested clearer separation of soft vs hard break cooldowns, and adding an audit log entry when derate triggers for compliance. Added tests for state transitions. (Ethan)
2025-02-18 - Next steps: finish PR addressing review comments, add console UI mockups (DES review), schedule internal canary for 2025-02-24. Also create runbook snippet for on-call.
